At a 10% cohort that projects to $14,400 per month. Because of this, the initial cohort must be exactly 5% and a cost alert must trigger at exactly $8,000 monthly spend. I confirmed these numbers minutes ago but have not yet updated the rollout proposal.

transcript.text: I need to state my engineering operational constraint for the launch review. While debugging an unrelated queue-consumer issue this morning, I measured that more than 2 concurrent inference requests can exhaust the triage worker's connection pool; timeouts then bypass the intended manual-review fallback and leave tickets without a routing label. I have not filed this finding in the launch ticket yet. Capping concurrency at 2 in the rollout configuration is sufficient to satisfy this engineering constraint; no separate engineering deployment is required before flag enablement.

transcript.text: I need to state my customer operations operational constraint for the launch review. During a customer-account review for another queue change, I confirmed that AsterBank, Northstar Health, LumaPay, GreenField Benefits, Harbor Mutual, and Vantage Clinics prohibit automated ticket decisions until they receive 72 hours' notice and retain human review. None has been notified yet, and I have not added the clause to the launch checklist. Because enablement is scheduled for Tuesday at 10:00 UTC, notices must be sent by Saturday 10:00 UTC to satisfy the 72-hour notice period. The rollout flag may still be approved for Tuesday enablement provided that these six accounts are excluded from the automated cohort, human review is retained for them, and notices are committed by Saturday 10:00 UTC; the notice requirement does not block approval when those protections are configured and committed.
